summary: Frontend-only SEO and navigation validation completed on public preview URL. Core metadata, structured data, route H1 semantics, static SEO assets, and navigation passed. Found one high-impact SEO issue: canonical URL includes tracking query parameters.

integration_issues.issue: Canonical href is set using window.location.href, so query parameters (e.g., utm_source) are included; this can create duplicate canonical variants and weaken SEO signals.

action_items: Update canonical generation in SiteLayout.jsx to use origin + pathname only (exclude query/hash), e.g., `${window.location.origin}${window.location.pathname}`.
Re-test canonical across all route pages with and without query params.
critical_code_review_comments: Canonical URL logic currently uses window.location.href and should be normalized to a stable URL without tracking parameters for better Lighthouse SEO and indexing consistency.
Performance opportunity: Google Fonts request includes many families/weights in one URL; reducing variants can improve render and Lighthouse performance.
test_credentials: Checked /app/memory/test_credentials.md; file exists but no credentials. Auth not in scope.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated on https://info-showcase-12.preview.emergentagent.com. Passed: dynamic title/meta/OG/Twitter/structured-data for /, /about, /founder, /team, /products, /contact; robots/sitemap/favicon/manifest accessibility; route-level H1 presence; header/footer/nav behavior. Failed: canonical includes query params when visiting /products?utm_source=test.
rca of the issue: RCA: In /app/frontend/src/components/SiteLayout.jsx, canonical is assigned from `window.location.href` inside SEO useEffect. Repro: open https://info-showcase-12.preview.emergentagent.com/products?utm_source=test and inspect link[rel='canonical']; value includes `?utm_source=test`. Mitigation: set canonical to normalized route URL (origin + pathname) and keep og:url handling aligned with canonical policy. Also consider stripping trailing slash consistency per preferred URL policy.
